answer: The cheapest real defence: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because beacon only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, ivory is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any sparrow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
